title: OTWD common definitions
description: Identifiers, codes, the provenance record and the record-level building blocks every OTWD v1 schema shares: the fact wrapper, status and closure fields, photos, the full and compact record envelopes with their lifecycle rule, derived values, attribution and GeoJSON shapes. This file defines no document of its own.

Ulid.description: A ULID in canonical form: 26 characters of Crockford base32, upper case.

SiteId.description: Stable public ID of a site. It never changes and is never reused. After a merge the losing site's ID redirects to the surviving site.

RoadRestrictionId.description: Stable public ID of a road restriction. It never changes and is never reused. After a merge the losing record's ID redirects to the surviving one.

RoadSegmentId.description: Stable public ID of a road segment. It never changes and is never reused. After a merge the losing record's ID redirects to the surviving one.

FerryServiceId.description: Stable public ID of a ferry service. It never changes and is never reused. After a merge the losing record's ID redirects to the surviving one.

RecordId.description: Stable public ID of any record. The kind segment names the record type, which is a code in the record type registry (record-types.json). The pattern accepts any record type code so a consumer written for an earlier minor version still reads IDs of record types added later, and skips records of a type it does not know. The kinds of OTWD's other identifiers are reserved and never name a record type. OTWD and its validator accept only registered record types (x-otwd-registry).

NonRecordId.description: An OTWD identifier whose kind is reserved for something other than a record: a submission, moderation decision, verdict, photo, upload, contributor, partner app, seed source, appeal or API key.

RecordType.description: The record type, as it appears in the kind segment of a record's public ID: a code in the record type registry (record-types.json). Open: a minor version can register a new record type, and a consumer skips records, changes and bulk downloads of a record type it does not know.

SubmissionId.description: ID of a submission, assigned by OTWD when the submission is received.

UploadId.description: ID of a photo upload slot created through the API, referenced by an add_photo submission.

ContributorId.description: OTWD's own public ID for a contributor. Signed-in contributors receive one at sign-in. Contributors who reach OTWD through a partner app receive one the first time the partner app sends their pseudonymous ID, and the pseudonymous ID itself is never published.

PartnerAppId.description: ID of a partner app, assigned when the partner app is registered.

SeedSourceId.description: ID of a seed source. Seed sources are curated by OTWD maintainers, so the ID is a readable slug that names the publisher and dataset.

ChangeSeq.description: A position in the change feed. Sequence numbers are global across all records, start at 1 and only increase.

SchemaVersion.description: The OTWD schema version a document follows. Minor versions only add optional fields and governed list entries.

RecordStatus.description: Whether a record is in use. A closed enumeration: a consumer decides what to show from it, so it gains a value only in a new major version. active: in use. temporarily_closed: a temporary closure, such as a site shut for repairs, a bridge closed after flood damage or a ferry service suspended. closed: a closure, such as a site that no longer operates, a road restriction removed when its structure was replaced, a road segment closed for good or a ferry service withdrawn. The record keeps its public ID and history. merged: the record was a duplicate and redirect_to names the survivor.

Code.description: A governed list code: lower case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. Codes are never renamed or reused.

EnumCode.description: A value of an open enumeration: lower case letters, digits and underscores. An open enumeration lists the values known at its schema version in x-otwd-known-values. OTWD only ever sends and accepts known values, and tools/validate.py holds producers to them, but a minor version can add values, so a consumer accepts any value that matches this pattern and follows the fallback the enumeration's description gives for one it does not know (ADR 0035).

SubmissionKind.description: The kind of a submission. Open: a consumer reading submission statuses or moderation decisions treats a kind it does not know as a submission it cannot show in detail. The API rejects a submission of a kind it does not accept with 422.

ModerationOutcome.description: The outcome of a moderation decision. approved: applied as submitted. edited_and_approved: applied after a moderator corrected it. rejected: not applied. needs_info: waiting for the contributor to answer the public note. Open: a consumer treats an outcome it does not know as not applied, unless the decision lists change_seqs.

SiteTypeCode.description: A code from the governed site type vocabulary (site-types.json). The pattern accepts codes added after this schema version so older validators keep working. Consumers ignore codes they do not recognise.

FacilityCode.description: A code from the governed facility vocabulary (facilities.json). The pattern accepts codes added after this schema version so older validators keep working. Consumers ignore codes they do not recognise.

StructureCode.description: A code from the governed structure vocabulary (structures.json). Consumers ignore codes they do not recognise.

SurfaceCode.description: A code from the governed surface vocabulary (surfaces.json). Consumers ignore codes they do not recognise.

VehicleAccessClassCode.description: A code from the governed vehicle access class vocabulary (vehicle-access-classes.json). Consumers treat a code they do not recognise as the most restrictive class.

VehicleClassCode.description: A code from the governed vehicle class vocabulary (vehicle-classes.json). Consumers ignore codes they do not recognise.

ReasonCode.description: A machine-readable reason in a verdict or a moderation decision, for example price_outlier or duplicate_of_existing_site.

FieldPointer.description: JSON Pointer to a fact or facility in a record, for example /facts/prices, /facts/vertical_clearance or /facilities/wifi. The part after /facilities/ is a facility code and follows Code. Only sites have facilities.

Sha256.description: SHA-256 of a file, hex encoded in lower case.

LanguageTag.description: A BCP 47 language tag, for example en, en-AU or pjt (Pitjantjatjara).

LocalisedText.description: A piece of text with the language it is written in.

Notes.description: Short free-text notes in one or more languages.

CountryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, upper case.

SubdivisionCode.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code, for example AU-NSW or NZ-CAN. The part before the hyphen is the country code.

Timestamp.description: An instant: an RFC 3339 date and time in UTC, with the Z suffix and no other offset, for example 2026-09-08T23:10:00Z. Every moment OTWD records (recorded_at, retrieved_at, decided_at, created_at, applied_at, the change feed and webhook payloads) uses it. Show it in the reader's own time zone. Local schedules such as opening hours never use it.

LocalDate.description: A local calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, read in the time zone of the record it belongs to: the day as people at the record count it, for example the day a closure began or a fact was observed. It is never converted to UTC.

TimeZone.description: IANA time zone name, for example Australia/Darwin. Local schedules (LocalTime, LocalDate, MonthDay) are read in it.

PhoneE164.description: Phone number in E.164 form: a plus sign, the country code and the national number, with no spaces.

LocalTime.description: Local clock time of day in 24-hour HH:MM form, read in the record's time zone or in the time_zone of the schedule that holds it. 24:00 means the end of the day. It is never converted to UTC: a 06:00 departure stays at 06:00 on the local clock when daylight saving starts or ends.

MonthDay.description: A day of the year in MM-DD form, used for periods that repeat every year. It is a local calendar day, read in the record's time zone or the schedule's own time_zone, and never converted to UTC.

SpdxLicence.description: SPDX licence identifier, or LicenseRef-<name> for a licence that SPDX does not list (for example a government open data licence).

SeedSourceRef.description: Details of the external open dataset a fact was imported from. The licence must be compatible with publishing the fact under CC BY 4.0.

dataset_name.description: The dataset's name as its publisher gives it.

publisher.description: The organisation that publishes the dataset.

attribution.description: The attribution statement the licence requires. Partner apps that display this fact must show it.

record_id.description: The record's own identifier inside the seed source, so the fact can be traced back.

dataset_version.description: Version or release date of the dataset as published.

Provenance.description: Who supplied a fact, through which partner app or seed source, when, and with what confidence. Every fact carries one. Every fact reaches the live data through a submission, a moderation decision and a change, including seed source imports, so all three are always named.

source_kind.description: contributor: a signed-in contributor supplied the fact directly. partner_app: a partner app supplied it, usually on behalf of one of its contributors. seed_source: it was imported from an open dataset. Open: a consumer treats a source kind it does not know as an unnamed source and still reads the fact's confidence.

observed_on.description: The date the fact was observed on the ground, or the date the seed source says the record was current. Older observations are less likely to be true today.

recorded_at.description: When OTWD applied the fact to the live data.

confidence.description: OTWD's estimate, from 0 to 1, that the fact is correct. It is computed from the source's trust score, the moderation route, the age of the observation and any later confirmations.

change_seq.description: The change that set this fact. Submissions are checked for conflicts against it.

moderator_edited.description: True when a moderator corrected the submitted value before approving it (outcome edited_and_approved). The decision records the original value.

Confirmations.description: Later reports that the fact is still true, without changing its value.

Fact.description: One fact in the full form of a record: its value beside its provenance, so the two always travel together. Every record type uses this wrapper and constrains value with the fact's own value shape, for example { "$ref": "common.schema.json#/$defs/Fact", "properties": { "value": { "$ref": "values.schema.json#/$defs/Names" } } }.

ClosureAuthority.description: The authority that declared a closure, such as a road authority closing a flood-damaged bridge.

ClosureInfoUrl.description: The authority's official page for a closure. Short incident closures belong there, not in OTWD.

StatusFact.description: The status of a record in the full form, with the reason for a closure and its provenance.

reason.description: Why the record is closed or temporarily closed.

reopens_on.description: For temporarily_closed: the expected reopening date, when known.

closed_on.description: For temporarily_closed or closed: the date the closure began, when known.

Photo.description: A published photo of a record, such as a site or the sign at a road restriction. Photos are licensed CC BY 4.0 by the person who took them, and EXIF location data is removed before publication.

url.description: HTTPS address of the full-size image on the OTWD CDN.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the published image file.

attribution.description: The credit to show with the photo, as the photographer chose it, for example a display name. Never an email address.

Photos.description: A record's published photos in the full form.

CompactPhotos.description: A record's published photos in the compact form: each photo without its provenance.

FullRecord.description: The envelope every record shares in the full form: identity, status, timestamps, change_seq and photos, with the lifecycle rule. A merged record is a stub that names the survivor in redirect_to. Any other record has derived values and facts, and no redirect_to. Each record type's schema narrows id and redirect_to to its own public ID kind and adds derived and facts.

redirect_to.description: For a merged record only: the public ID of the surviving record, of the same record type. The API answers requests for this record with a 301 redirect to it.

updated_at.description: When the latest change to this record was applied.

change_seq.description: Sequence number of the latest change applied to this record. A submission that changes the record sends it back as base_change_seq so conflicts can be detected.

CompactRecord.description: The envelope every record shares in the compact form: identity, status with the closure fields flattened, timestamps, the primary name, photos, and the attribution list, min_confidence and safety_facts_observed_on that stand in for per-fact provenance. A merged record names the survivor in redirect_to, and no other record has one. Each compact schema narrows id and redirect_to, adds its derived values and facts, and lists the fields its record type always has when it is not merged.

name.description: The primary name, copied from names for convenience.

PointDerivedValues.description: The values OTWD computes from the location of a site or road restriction using boundary datasets. Contributors never submit them, so they carry no provenance of their own, and they are recomputed whenever the location changes. The full form holds them in derived (PointDerived), and the compact form at the top level.

locality.description: The nearest town or suburb name, for display and web addresses.

PointDerived.description: The derived object of a point record in the full form.

CountryCodes.description: The countries a line passes through.

SubdivisionCodes.description: The subdivisions a line passes through.

Localities.description: Town or suburb names along a line, in order from its start, for display.

TimeZones.description: Every IANA time zone the line passes through, in order from its start, so the first is time_zone. A zone appears again each time the line returns to it, as on a track from South Australia into Victoria and back, but never twice in a row (tools/validate.py checks this). A schedule's own time_zone must be one of them.

LengthKm.description: Length of a line's geometry along the ground, in kilometres.

LineDerivedValues.description: The values OTWD computes from the geometry of a road segment or ferry service. Contributors never submit them, so they carry no provenance of their own, and they are recomputed whenever the geometry changes. A line can cross a border, so countries and subdivisions are lists. The full form holds them in derived (LineDerived), and the compact form at the top level.

time_zone.description: The record's default time zone: the zone at the start of the line. Local times and dates in the record's facts are read in it, unless a schedule names its own time_zone.

LineDerived.description: The derived object of a line record in the full form.

AttributionList.description: Every credit a record's facts require, in the compact form. The first entry is always the Open Touring credit. Seed source credits follow, once each.

MinConfidence.description: The lowest confidence of any fact on the record, so a reader of the compact form can tell when to fetch the full form.

SafetyFactsObservedOn.description: The oldest observed date among the record's safety facts, when known. Apps can warn when it is old.

Position.description: A GeoJSON position (RFC 7946): longitude then latitude in WGS84 decimal degrees. OTWD positions have no altitude.

GeoJsonPoint.description: A GeoJSON Point geometry (RFC 7946) in WGS84. Bulk downloads and GeoJSON responses use it for sites and road restrictions, built from the location fact.

GeoJsonLineString.description: A GeoJSON LineString geometry (RFC 7946) in WGS84, with at least two positions.

GeoJsonMultiLineString.description: A GeoJSON MultiLineString geometry (RFC 7946) in WGS84: several lines that together make one record, such as the two carriageways of a divided road.
